answer: A bond is posted against a hardware root, so one device backs one identity. Submit the same text twice and the bond is forfeited to the auditor pool that caught it. A thousand-account farm needs a thousand roots or it loses the bond on the first duplicate. The fable of cheap sybils ends there: hardware costs money, duplicates cost the bond, and the mirror of the ledger keeps both. What stays out of reach is the horizon: one device still means one identity, so the next thousand bonds cost exactly as much as the first.
